[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This playbook defines the end-to-end architecture pipeline — the ordered sequence of commands that takes a project from discovery through implementation-ready specifications. It provides the authoritative execution path, decision points, and quality gates for producing traceable, BDD-driven architecture artifacts.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- Eliminates ambiguity about what to run and when — architects and engineers follow one path
- Produces fully traceable artifacts: every implementation issue traces back to a requirement, ADR, and bounded context
- Enables maximum concurrency in implementation by decomposing work into dependency-ordered, parallelizable features
- Supports both greenfield and brownfield (reverse engineering) workflows through the same pipeline

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#problem-description]

#### Problem Description

Without a defined execution order, teams run commands out of sequence (e.g., exporting issues before logical architecture exists), producing incomplete issues that lack ADR constraints and tech-spec references. This causes rework when implementation agents discover missing guardrails.

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#principle-1-immutable-artifact-chain]

#### Principle 1: Immutable Artifact Chain

**Description:** Each pipeline stage produces artifacts that downstream stages consume but never modify.
**Rationale:** Traceability breaks if upstream artifacts are silently edited after downstream work begins.
**Application:** Once a stage completes, its artifacts are frozen. Changes require re-running the stage and cascading updates downstream.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#principle-2-human-gates-at-architecture-decisions]

#### Principle 2: Human Gates at Architecture Decisions

**Description:** CRB (conceptual) and ARB (logical) reviews are human approval gates — the pipeline pauses until approval.
**Rationale:** Architecture decisions have long-lived consequences. AI proposes; humans approve.
**Application:** `/eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create` produces a CRB submission. The pipeline does not proceed to `/eap-spec-fr-create` until CRB approves. Similarly, logical architecture requires ARB approval before NFR creation.
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#principle-3-bdd-as-the-single-source-of-truth]

#### Principle 3: BDD as the Single Source of Truth

**Description:** `.feature` files are the specification — everything else (issues, stories, plans) is derived from them.
**Rationale:** A single authoritative source eliminates drift between what's specified and what's tracked.
**Application:** Never hand-author GitHub Issues or ADO Stories for implementation — always generate them from specs via `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` or `/eap-decom-spec-export-boards --stories`.

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#approach-1-forward-engineering-greenfield]

#### Approach 1: Forward Engineering (Greenfield)

**Overview:** Start from business intent, design architecture, decompose into specs, export to execution.
**When to Use:** New systems, new bounded contexts, or major capability additions with no existing code.
**Implementation:** Execute the required pipeline stages in order (Stages 6→11).
**Benefits:** Clean traceability, no legacy debt to reconcile.
**Considerations:** Requires clear business sponsorship and domain expertise for conceptual architecture.
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#approach-2-reverse-then-forward-brownfield]

#### Approach 2: Reverse-then-Forward (Brownfield)

**Overview:** Extract knowledge from existing code, validate with SMEs, then feed into the forward pipeline.
**When to Use:** Modernization of existing systems, migration from legacy platforms.
**Implementation:** Execute optional reverse engineering (Stages 1→5), then continue with the required pipeline.
**Benefits:** Preserves institutional knowledge, surfaces undocumented business rules.
**Considerations:** RE phases are time-intensive; `/eap-disc-re-deepen` alone can take 5-15x longer than discovery.
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#best-practice-1-run-eap-sdd-health-check-after-every-major-stage]

#### Best Practice 1: Run `/eap-sdd-health-check` After Every Major Stage

**Description:** Don't wait until the end to validate — run health checks incrementally.
**Rationale:** Catching a missing artifact at Stage 7 is cheaper than discovering it at Stage 11.
**Implementation:** After completing `/eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create`, `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create`, and `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues`, run `/eap-sdd-health-check` to validate accumulated artifacts.
**Success Indicators:** Health check passes with no missing-artifact warnings.
page_texts.31:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#best-practice-2-derive-requirements-before-writing-specs]

#### Best Practice 2: Derive Requirements Before Writing Specs

**Description:** When regulatory or legacy sources exist, run `/eap-disc-requirements-derive` + `/eap-disc-requirements-synthesize` before `/eap-spec-fr-create`.
**Rationale:** Pre-derived rules auto-populate the Example Mapping session, reducing spec creation time by 40-60%.
**Implementation:** Point `/eap-disc-requirements-derive` at CFR documents or legacy code, synthesize, then `/eap-spec-fr-create` consumes the `_decisions.md` output.
**Success Indicators:** Feature files reference `DEC-####` decision IDs in their Rule: statements.
page_texts.33:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#pitfall-1-exporting-issues-before-logical-architecture]

#### Pitfall 1: Exporting Issues Before Logical Architecture

**Description:** Running `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` before `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create` completes.
**Impact:** Issues lack ADR constraints and tech-spec references — agents implement without guardrails.
**Prevention:** Follow the required ordering. `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` requires `docs/design/tech-specs.md` to exist.
**Mitigation:** Re-run `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` after logical architecture is complete; it will patch existing issues.
page_texts.34:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#pitfall-2-skipping-nfrs-for-simple-projects]

#### Pitfall 2: Skipping NFRs for "Simple" Projects

**Description:** Assuming non-functional requirements aren't needed because the domain is straightforward.
**Impact:** Performance, security, and operational concerns surface during implementation as unplanned work.
**Prevention:** `/eap-spec-nfr-create` is a required stage. The logical architecture's Quality Attributes section (Phase 8) provides the input — if it's thin, the problem is upstream.
**Mitigation:** Return to `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create` and flesh out Quality Attributes before proceeding.

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#phase-1-discovery-and-conceptual-design]

#### Phase 1: Discovery and Conceptual Design

**Objectives:** Establish bounded contexts, domain vocabulary, and system purpose.
**Prerequisites:** Business intent or legacy codebase available.
**Key Activities:**

1. (Optional) Run reverse engineering pipeline on existing code
2. Execute `/eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create` to produce BDD-ready conceptual architecture
3. Submit CRB input document for review
4. Obtain CRB approval before proceeding

**Deliverables:**

| Artifact | Location | Purpose |
| -------- | -------- | ------- |
| Conceptual Architecture | `docs/design/conceptual/<slug>.md` | Bounded contexts, capabilities, glossary |
| CRB Submission | `docs/design/conceptual/<slug>-crb-input.md` | Formal review input |
| Context Diagrams | `docs/design/conceptual/assets/*.drawio.svg` | Visual architecture (C4 L1, L2, process) |

**Success Criteria:** CRB approval obtained; `/eap-sdd-health-check` reports conceptual artifacts present.
page_texts.45:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#phase-2-specification]

#### Phase 2: Specification

**Objectives:** Decompose capabilities into testable BDD scenarios and quality attributes.
**Prerequisites:** Approved conceptual architecture.
**Key Activities:**

1. (Optional) Run `/eap-disc-requirements-derive` + `/eap-disc-requirements-synthesize` on regulatory/legacy sources
2. Execute `/eap-spec-fr-create` for each business capability (run per concern)
3. Execute `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create` to define technical architecture
4. Submit ARB input document for review; obtain ARB approval
5. Execute `/eap-spec-nfr-create` to define quality attribute scenarios

**Deliverables:**

| Artifact | Location | Purpose |
| -------- | -------- | ------- |
| Functional Specs | `docs/requirements/functional/<concern>/*.feature` | BDD scenarios (3–15 per file) |
| Logical Architecture | `docs/design/logical/<slug>.md` | Component, data, integration, security design |
| ADRs | `docs/decisions/adr-<N>-<slug>.md` | Architecture decision records |
| Tech Specs | `docs/design/tech-specs.md` | Verifiable implementation constraints |
| Non-functional Specs | `docs/requirements/non-functional/<concern>/*.feature` | Quality attribute scenarios |
| Traceability Matrix | `docs/requirements/traceability.md` | Cross-reference of all tags to artifacts |

**Success Criteria:** ARB approval obtained; traceability matrix populated for all `@FR-*` and `@NFR-*` tags.
page_texts.46:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#phase-3-export-and-planning]

#### Phase 3: Export and Planning

**Objectives:** Convert specifications into actionable work items with dependency ordering.
**Prerequisites:** All specifications complete; logical architecture approved.
**Key Activities:**

1. Execute `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` to generate GitHub Issues with full constraint chains
2. Execute `/eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence` to produce dependency DAG and phase ordering
3. (Optional) Execute `/eap-decom-spec-export-boards --stories` to create ADO User Stories for business planning
4. (Optional) Execute `/eap-guide-create` for developer guides on key concerns
5. Execute `/eap-sdd-health-check` as the final validation gate

**Deliverables:**

| Artifact | Location | Purpose |
| -------- | -------- | ------- |
| GitHub Issues | Repository Issues tab | Agent-ready implementation tasks (3 per feature) |
| Project Plan | `docs/project-plan.md` | Phases, DAG, concurrency guide, critical path |
| ADO Stories (opt) | ADO Backlog | Business planning layer |
| Developer Guides (opt) | `docs/guides/<concern>/README.md` | Implementation guidance for engineers |
| Health Check Report | Console output | Final pipeline integrity validation |

**Success Criteria:** `/eap-sdd-health-check` passes all categories; project plan shows ≥3 concurrent features per phase.
page_texts.48:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#critical-success-factor-1-strict-stage-ordering]

#### Critical Success Factor 1: Strict Stage Ordering

**Description:** Never skip or reorder required stages — each stage's outputs are inputs to the next.
**Importance:** A single missing artifact (e.g., tech-specs.md) cascades into dozens of incomplete issues.
**Implementation:** Follow the pipeline diagram exactly. Use `/eap-sdd-health-check` to verify intermediate state.
**Measurement:** Zero "missing artifact" warnings from health check at pipeline completion.
page_texts.49:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#critical-success-factor-2-human-approval-at-gates]

#### Critical Success Factor 2: Human Approval at Gates

**Description:** CRB and ARB gates require human sign-off before the pipeline advances.
**Importance:** Architecture decisions affect years of maintenance — AI proposes, humans govern.
**Implementation:** Generate CRB/ARB input documents; schedule reviews; do not proceed without approval.
**Measurement:** All projects have documented CRB/ARB approval before specification phases.

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#preparation-steps]

#### Preparation Steps

1. **Validate Environment**

    - Run `task health` to confirm tooling
    - Run `/eap-env-health-check` to verify Claude Code configuration
    - Confirm MCP servers respond (GitHub + ADO)

2. **Identify Pipeline Entry Point**

    - If modernizing existing code → start at `/eap-disc-re-survey` (Stage 1)
    - If greenfield with regulatory sources → start at `/eap-disc-requirements-derive`, then `/eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create`
    - If greenfield with clear business intent → start at `/eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create` (Stage 6)
page_texts.53:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#execution-steps]

#### Execution Steps

1. **Stage 6 — Conceptual Architecture** (Required)

    ```text
    /eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create
    ```
    - Input: Business intent, domain knowledge, (optional) RE outputs
    - Output: Conceptual doc, CRB submission, 3 diagrams
    - Gate: **CRB Approval** — pause until approved

2. **Stage 7 — Functional Requirements** (Required, run per concern)

    ```text
    /eap-spec-fr-create
    ```
    - Input: Approved conceptual architecture, (optional) derived requirements
    - Output: `.feature` files, traceability entries, ADO User Story
    - Note: Run once per business capability/concern

3. **Stage 8 — Logical Architecture** (Required)

    ```text
    /eap-decom-logical-arch-create
    ```
    - Input: Conceptual architecture, functional specs (for traceability)
    - Output: Logical doc, ADRs, tech-specs.md, ARB submission, 4 diagrams
    - Gate: **ARB Approval** — pause until approved

4. **Stage 9 — Non-Functional Requirements** (Required)

    ```text
    /eap-spec-nfr-create
    ```
    - Input: Approved logical architecture (Quality Attributes section)
    - Output: NFR `.feature` files, systemic NFR docs, traceability entries

5. **Stage 10 — Export Issues** (Required)

    ```text
    /eap-decom-spec-export-issues
    ```
    - Input: All `.feature` files, tech-specs.md, traceability matrix
    - Output: GitHub Issues (implementation + testing + infrastructure per feature)
    - Note: Issues include full constraint chains and ADR references

6. **Stage 11 — Plan Sequence** (Required)

    ```text
    /eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence
    ```
    - Input: Functional/NFR specs, conceptual architecture
    - Output: `docs/project-plan.md` with phases, DAG, concurrency guide

7. **Final Gate — Architecture Health Check** (Required)

    ```text
    /eap-sdd-health-check
    ```
    - Input: All accumulated artifacts
    - Output: Pass/Fail report across all validation categories
page_texts.54:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#validation-steps]

#### Validation Steps

1. **Verify Traceability Completeness**
    - Open `docs/requirements/traceability.md`
    - Confirm every `@FR-*` and `@NFR-*` tag has GH# and (optionally) AB# mappings
    - Confirm ADR column is populated per governing decisions

2. **Verify Issue Quality**
    - Spot-check 3-5 GitHub Issues
    - Confirm each has: Goal, Acceptance Criteria, Constraints (with tech-spec references), Enterprise Work Item
    - Confirm dependency tiers (T1/T2/T3) are annotated

3. **Verify Plan Feasibility**
    - Open `docs/project-plan.md`
    - Confirm critical path is identified
    - Confirm no circular dependencies exist
    - Confirm concurrency score meets target (≥3 features per phase)

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#decision-point-1-when-to-use-reverse-engineering]

#### Decision Point 1: When to Use Reverse Engineering

**Context:** A legacy system exists that will be modernized or replaced.
**Options:**
- Full RE pipeline (5 stages): Legacy code is complex, poorly documented, 100k+ LOC
- Partial RE (discover + extract only): Code is moderately documented, <50k LOC
- Skip RE entirely: Business intent is well-understood, no legacy to preserve

**Criteria:** LOC count, documentation quality, SME availability, timeline pressure.
**Recommendation:** If >50k LOC with undocumented business rules, run full RE. Otherwise, skip.
page_texts.57:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#decision-point-2-when-to-use-requirements-engineering]

#### Decision Point 2: When to Use Requirements Engineering

**Context:** External authoritative sources exist (regulations, contracts, legacy specs).
**Options:**
- Run `/eap-disc-requirements-derive` + `/eap-disc-requirements-synthesize`: Multiple sources must be reconciled
- Run `/eap-disc-requirements-derive` only: Single source, no conflicts to resolve
- Skip entirely: Business intent is conversational, no formal source documents

**Criteria:** Number of source documents, regulatory complexity, conflict likelihood.
**Recommendation:** If CFR/HIPAA references exist, always derive. If only verbal requirements, skip.

#### Techniques and Methods

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#template-2-github-issue-structure]

#### Template 2: GitHub Issue Structure

**Purpose:** Agent-ready implementation task produced by `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues`
**Location:** GitHub repository Issues tab

```markdown
## Goal
{What to deliver}

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Scenario: {scenario name} passes
- [ ] All tests green
- [ ] Lint clean
- [ ] Coverage ≥90%

## Constraints
- **Feature file:** `docs/requirements/functional/{concern}/{file}.feature`
- **Scope boundary:** `components/<target>/src/{concern}/`
- **Governing ADRs:** ADR-{N} ({title})
- **Tech-spec constraints:** TS-{DOMAIN}-{NNN}
- **Cross-BC deps (T1):** #{issue} must be DONE
- **Cross-BC deps (T2):** #{issue} interface must EXIST
- **Enterprise artifacts:** STD-*, PTN-*, GUID-*

## Enterprise Work Item
AB#{XXXXX}
```

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#use-case-1-greenfield-microservice]

#### Use Case 1: Greenfield Microservice

**Scenario Description:** A new claims processing service with 5 bounded contexts.
**Context:** Clear business requirements from PO; no existing code; HIPAA compliance required.
**Guidance Application:**
1. Skip RE stages (no legacy code)
2. `/eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create` → 5 bounded contexts identified, CRB approved
3. `/eap-disc-requirements-derive` from 42 CFR Part 447 → 23 requirement candidates
4. `/eap-disc-requirements-synthesize` → 18 unique requirements with 3 conflicts resolved
5. `/eap-spec-fr-create` × 12 capabilities → 47 `.feature` files
6. `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create` → 7 ADRs, 34 tech-spec constraints, ARB approved
7. `/eap-spec-nfr-create` → 8 NFR features, 3 systemic NFR docs
8. `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` → 141 GitHub Issues (47 impl + 47 test + 47 infra)
9. `/eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence` → 4 phases, critical path = 6 features, max concurrency = 8
10. `/eap-sdd-health-check` → PASS

**Success Factors:** Early CRB/ARB engagement; requirements derivation from CFR saved rework.
page_texts.67:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#use-case-2-legacy-system-modernization]

#### Use Case 2: Legacy System Modernization

**Scenario Description:** Migrating a 200k LOC COBOL/C# eligibility system.
**Context:** Minimal documentation; 3 SMEs available part-time; 18-month timeline.
**Guidance Application:**
1. `/eap-disc-re-survey` → 42 capabilities, 156 structural contracts identified
2. `/eap-disc-re-extract` → 89 business rules, 234 behavioral scenarios, 67 DB procedures
3. `/eap-disc-re-deepen` → 1,200+ detailed rules, event catalog with 45 domain events
4. `/eap-disc-re-validate` → PASS (87% observed confidence, 12x extraction multiplier)
5. `/eap-disc-re-review` → 156 REVW cards generated; SMEs dispositioned 142 (91%)
6. Continue with forward pipeline (Stages 6→11) using RE outputs as domain input

**Success Factors:** SME availability for review stage; patience with `/eap-disc-re-deepen` duration.

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#exception-handling]

#### Exception Handling

- **CRB/ARB rejection**: Address feedback, re-run the relevant `/create` command, resubmit
- **Health check failure**: Identify missing artifacts, re-run the stage that produces them
- **Partial pipeline**: If only functional specs are needed (e.g., adding a single feature to existing architecture), run from `/eap-spec-fr-create` with `--skip-validation` — but accept that issue quality will be lower

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-010-architecture-pipeline-playbook.md#risk-assessment]

#### Risk Assessment

| Risk Category | Risk Description | Probability | Impact | Mitigation Strategy |
| ------------- | ---------------- | ----------- | ------ | ------------------- |
| Incomplete Specs | Features exported before all scenarios written | Medium | High | `/eap-sdd-health-check` blocks on traceability gaps |
| Stale Issues | Specs change after issues created | Medium | Medium | Re-run `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` to patch |
| Dependency Errors | Wrong tier classification causes blocking | Low | High | `/eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence` validates DAG acyclicity |
| Gate Delays | CRB/ARB availability delays pipeline | Medium | Medium | Submit early; pipeline allows spec work in parallel with ARB review |

### Maturity Model

| Maturity Level | Description | Characteristics | Next Steps |
| -------------- | ----------- | --------------- | ---------- |
| Level 1: Ad-hoc | Commands run sporadically | Missing stages, incomplete artifacts, manual issue creation | Adopt required ordering; run `/eap-sdd-health-check` |
| Level 2: Defined | Full pipeline executed per project | All required stages complete; gates observed | Add optional stages; measure cycle time |
| Level 3: Managed | Metrics tracked, reconciliation active | `/eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence --reconcile` runs regularly; rework <15% | Automate gate notifications |
| Level 4: Optimized | Pipeline adapts per project context | Dynamic entry points; interface-first acceleration used | Continuous feedback into command improvements |
